key_insight: DeepEvidence shifts AI research assistance from simple fact retrieval to active evidence exploration and synthesis. Instead of returning isolated answers, it builds explicit representations of scientific evidence to support deeper biomedical discovery.
problem_solved: Traditional knowledge-retrieval systems can find relevant facts, but they struggle to organize, compare, and interpret evidence across many studies. This paper addresses the bottleneck of turning scattered biomedical information into usable scientific understanding.
method: Introduces DeepEvidence, a deep research agent designed for evidence exploration rather than only document lookup.
Constructs explicit representations of scientific evidence to connect claims, support, and context across sources.
Supports synthesis of retrieved information into a more structured, research-oriented view of the literature.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a shift from search-focused assistants to agents that can reason over evidence and help generate scientific understanding. It is especially relevant for building tools for literature review, biomedical decision support, and research discovery.

paper_title: Shifting from knowledge retrieval to evidence exploration and synthesis
paper_authors: Shruti Shikhare, Jake Cohen-Setton, Krishna C. Bulusu
